**Question:** Should `--ttl` accept any whole number of seconds at or above 1, or should there be a documented maximum that a larger value is rejected against? (FR-033)

Why it matters: with no upper limit an administrator can issue a token with a lifetime of a thousand years, which quietly turns a short-lived recovery credential into a permanent second password for the account.

**Recommended:** Option B — The expiry window is what makes handing a token to someone out of band acceptable, so it should have a stated ceiling; 24 hours is generous for passing a token to a user by phone or in person. Rejecting an over-large value with the existing usage line and exit 2 matches how FR-033 already treats every other bad `--ttl` and satisfies Principle II's "fail loudly", whereas silently clamping would hide the fact that the administrator did not get the lifetime they asked for.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | No maximum — any whole number of seconds at or above 1 is accepted. (current spec) |
| B | Maximum 86400 seconds (24 hours); a larger value is a malformed invocation — usage line on stderr, exit 2, store untouched. |
| C | Maximum 604800 seconds (7 days), rejected the same way above that. |
| D | No maximum, but a value above the ceiling is silently clamped to it. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
